name: Cream Méringues
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: eggs (the whites only), whipped stiff, with 1 lb. powdered sugar
ingredients.originalText: 4 eggs (the whites only), whipped stiff, with 1 lb. powdered sugar

instructions.text: When very stiff, heap in the shape of half an egg upon stiff letter-paper lining the bottom of your baking-pan
Have them half an inch apart
Do not shut the oven-door closely, but leave a space through which you can watch them
When they are a light yellow-brown, take them out and cool quickly
Slip a thin-bladed knife under each; scoop out the soft inside, and fill with cream whipped as for Charlotte Russe

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. When very stiff, heap in the shape of half an egg upon stiff letter-paper lining the bottom of your baking-pan
2. Have them half an inch apart
3. Do not shut the oven-door closely, but leave a space through which you can watch them
4. When they are a light yellow-brown, take them out and cool quickly
5. Slip a thin-bladed knife under each; scoop out the soft inside, and fill with cream whipped as for Charlotte Russe
